spec.title: theia PROP-005: Upgrade advisory, hygiene, conventions

status.comment: answers to TYPE-AREA-ADVISORY, TYPE-AREA-CONVENTIONS; facts 01, 07, 08; implemented in P5 - six advisory readers, the hygiene rules as the reminders of the feature generator, the subsystems and the empty forbidden list

facts.THEIA-ADVISORY-READERS: Between two pins the advisory reads: the version of `lerna.json`; the Node engine of the root `package.json`; the Electron version pinned by `dev-packages/electron` (or the application's dev dependency); the set of `@theia/*` packages (added, removed, renamed - the removal of `@theia/preview` at master is the live example); the entry kinds of `theiaExtensions` in `extension-package.ts`; the `theia` section schema in `application-props.ts` (new or removed keys). Each is a semantic change with a recommendation, in the engine's frame. **Implemented in P5** as six readers: `monorepo-version` (`lerna.json`), `node-engine` (the root manifest), `workspace-packages` (the names of the workspace members, read from `package-lock.json`, which is where they are written machine-readably), `extension-entry-kinds` (the members of the `Extension` interface of `extension-package.ts`), `application-schema` (the property names of `application-props.ts`) and `application-electron` (the Electron version and the target of the application manifest). The Electron version lives in the application's dev dependencies and not in a `dev-packages/electron` package, which does not exist at this version - measured on the clone.

facts.THEIA-HEADER-RULE: Upstream's lint requires in every source file of a linted package a header matching `SPDX-License-Identifier: EPL-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only WITH Classpath-exception-2.0` (`configs/errors.eslintrc.json:105-115`, tslint `file-header`). An own package that carries the product's own licence therefore either carries a header the rule accepts or ships its own `.eslintrc.js` that overrides the rule for that package - the second is the product's choice, and it is a file of the own package, not a graft (`08-hygiene-and-lint.md`).
facts.THEIA-LOCALIZATION-RULE: `@theia/localization-check` forbids `nls.localizeByDefault` for a string that is not a VS Code message; own strings use `nls.localize(key, default)` with own keys, and the product's translations go into its own `nls.*.json` files or into the package's `i18n` the way `packages/core/i18n` does (`07-localization.md`). This is the type's answer to the string funnel: there is no `nls.ts` graft.
facts.THEIA-IMPORT-RULES: `@theia/runtime-import-check` (a closed set of folders and a fixed import lattice between `common`, `browser`, `node`, `electron-*`) and `@theia/shared-dependencies` (import inversify and other shared libraries only through `@theia/core/shared/*`) shape the layout of an own package: the same folder names, the same import direction, or the lint refuses (`08`).

facts.THEIA-SUBSYSTEMS: Subsystems for intervention ids: `core`, `frontend`, `backend`, `electron`, `plugin`, `app`, `build`, `test`, `deps`; id pattern `CK-(core|frontend|backend|electron|plugin|app|build|test|deps)-[0-9]{3}`.
facts.THEIA-FORBIDDEN-SERVICES: `forbiddenServiceIds` starts empty; there is no upstream list of services set before the container exists. Candidates appear from measurement of failed `rebind`s and are added with the failure that proved them.
